Disability not recorded - Assessment not completed

annotationMap.I: ".." denotes a nil or negligible number of claimants or award amount based on a nil or negligible number of claimants.
annotationMap.II: From March 2022, a new benefit called Adult Disability Payment (ADP) began to be introduced in Scotland. All Scottish applications for support because of disability or long term ill-health should be made to ADP from 29th August 2022. Social Security Scotland began to move clients to ADP from September 2022, and completed this case transfer process for those who were in receipt of PIP in Scotland by the end of June 2025.
annotationMap.III: Retrieving "DWP Ownership" returns claims administered by DWP in England, Wales and Abroad. Retrieving "Devolved to Scotland" returns claims DWP still administer in Scotland. From July 2025 onwards, any data appearing in Stat-Xplore for PIP activity in Scotland may relate to cases where a person moves to Scotland from England or Wales while in receipt of PIP and is in the process of applying for ADP instead. New legislation introduced in November 2025 provides for an extension of entitlement to PIP (commonly referred to as a "run-on period") of up to 13 weeks from the date of the move.
annotationMap.IV: Please note: If you retrieve all data within this benefit, this will return PIP claims administered by DWP. Datapoints from March 2022 will no longer reflect a full total for Great Britain because of the introduction of Adult Disability Payment in Scotland.
annotationMap.XI: For a very small proportion of the caseload (0.2%), the combination of award rates (daily living and mobility) is reported as nil-nil. Investigations suggest that award rates may be temporarily shown as a nil rate in the data used to derive the statistics for a short period, whilst a claim review is in process, after which the new award rate is set. These cases should be treated with caution and may be revised in a subsequent release.
annotationMap.VII: From March 2021 cases can be classified as "Coronavirus covid-19" on the PIP Computer System, which appears within Infectious Diseases > Viral Diseases. These cases are long covid / post-covid syndrome cases rather than initial covid-19 infection. Any individuals with long covid as their primary reason for claiming PIP prior to March 2021 will not be classified as "Coronavirus covid-19". These cases will remain classified according to their main symptoms (respiratory illness, fatigue etc.)
annotationMap.VIII: Operational measures implemented in late March 2020 in response to COVID-19 included the suspension of routine re-assessments and reviews of disability benefits – i.e. DLA to PIP reassessments and routine award reviews for those already claiming PIP. All PIP award reviews and DLA to PIP reassessments which had not yet had an assessment booked were delayed and existing awards due to expire were automatically extended to ensure continuity of financial support. Planned award reviews and some DLA reassessment activity resumed during July 2020.
annotationMap.V: Geographies are based on the claimants latest recorded address.  In some cases this may not be in the same geographical area as their initial claim.
annotationMap.X: From June 2024, cases classified as “Chronic Fatigue Syndrome” (CFS) on the PIP Computer System have been moved to Neurological Disease > Other neurological disorders. This change has been applied to all data from April 2013 onwards. In earlier published versions of the data, CFS cases were classified as Musculoskeletal disease (general) > Chronic pain syndromes.
